objective: Evaluate the proposed FastAPI supported-version range without changing the installed lockfile, API behavior, scientific contracts, or frozen baselines.

previous_knowledge_consumed.detail: The PR changes the FastAPI lower/upper version range from >=0.141.1,<0.143 to >=0.141.1,<0.164. It does not change application source code.
The lockfile still pins fastapi==0.141.1 and starlette==1.7.0. The default locked CI environment therefore does not by itself test the newly permitted upper range.
Format and lint passed. The cumulative lifecycle gate failed because the PR did not include a cycle record. Test Suite, Runtime Smoke, package build and Dependency Audit were skipped.

baseline.description: FastAPI dependency range is restricted to >=0.141.1,<0.143. The existing requirements lock pins FastAPI 0.141.1 and Starlette 1.7.0.

change.scope: Add only a machine-readable lifecycle record for the proposed FastAPI range change. No dependency version, lockfile, application code, API contract, model, feature schema, benchmark, or release artifact is changed by this commit.
change.rationale: The lifecycle gate correctly requires an auditable record. The record explicitly keeps the wider dependency range unverified until compatibility tests cover the declared supported versions.

expected_improvement: Make the proposed dependency-range change auditable.
Enable the repository's required CI stages to run after lifecycle validation.
Verify whether the wider FastAPI range remains compatible with the pinned Starlette range and the application API.

reliability.before: The FastAPI package metadata allows only >=0.141.1,<0.143. CI has not completed on the proposed wider range because the lifecycle gate stopped first.
reliability.after: The PR proposes >=0.141.1,<0.164. The locked environment still uses FastAPI 0.141.1, so compatibility at newer allowed versions requires an explicit test matrix before acceptance.

reproducibility.before: The PR had no machine-readable cycle record; the lifecycle gate rejected it.
reproducibility.after: A schema 1.1 cycle record is added. The next CI run must validate the record and run the full test, smoke, build and dependency stages.

measurement.trade_off: The wider version range can reduce future packaging conflicts, but it also permits untested FastAPI versions unless a compatibility matrix or upper-bound policy is established.

evidence: PR #298 changes only the FastAPI range in pyproject.toml.
requirements.lock still pins fastapi==0.141.1 and starlette==1.7.0.
CI #44721790514 passed Format and Lint, then stopped at the cycle-record requirement.
validation.blocker: Run CI after the cycle record is added. Separately test the current supported minimum and a suitably selected upper version from the declared FastAPI range, including Starlette compatibility, API tests, runtime smoke, package build, and dependency audit.

root_causes: The cumulative lifecycle gate rejected the PR because pyproject.toml changed without a JSON cycle record under configs/process/cycles/.
unresolved: The PR's wider FastAPI range is not validated by the current lockfile, which still pins FastAPI 0.141.1.
Compatibility with the declared Starlette constraint at newer FastAPI versions has not been measured.

findings: A permissive package version range is a compatibility claim. A locked test environment at the minimum version does not validate the full range.
FastAPI and Starlette compatibility must be tested together.
The CI lifecycle gate requires a change record before expensive or broad tests run.

open_blockers: Complete current-head CI after the cycle record is added.
Test at least one newer FastAPI version allowed by the proposed upper bound with its compatible Starlette release.
Run API contract tests, runtime smoke, package build and dependency audit.
Do not treat the dependency change as accepted until all checks pass.

knowledge_carried_forward: This cycle records the proposal and CI blocker only. It does not accept the wider FastAPI range.
Do not modify the frozen v0.2.0 scientific baseline, model, features, taxonomy, class order, or benchmark.
Keep PR #298 open until version-matrix evidence and all required checks pass.
